characters.description: One of Lori's schoolmates and her one-sided rival. Ascended Extra: She has a speaking role in "Selfie Improvement", where she is also the main drive of the plot. She is also a major character in "Senior Moment". Broken Ace: Despite besting Lori at almost everything, she is quite insecure. She actually thinks that Lori is better than her and envies her status as an elder sibling. Class Princess: Carol was voted homecoming queen over Lori, meaning she is quite popular, more so than Lori. Lori’s jealousy makes her view Carol as someone deliberately trying to outdo her, but she soon finds out Carol is genuinely nice, and actually envies Lori for her hair, her family, and her golf skills. Competition Freak: Her initial shtick towards Lori in terms of selfies.

characters.name: Chaz
characters.description: One of Lori's friends and Leni's first love interest in "L is for Love" (before they presumably broke up prior toThe Loud House Movie). He is shown to be a fashion designer. Birds of a Feather: What draws him and Leni together is the fact that both have an interest in fashion. Camp Straight: He likes fashion, which is typically considered to be feminine. That said, he definitely like girls, especially Leni. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He has not been heard from on the series since the episode "Really Loud Music", where it is implied that he is dating Leni.They are still in contact with each other as of the graphic novelLucy Rolls the Dice. Distaff Counterpart: Essentially a male version of Leni as both of them are fashion-obsesseddim-but-nice people.

characters.name: Fiona
characters.description: A friend of Leni's from Reininger's. Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: The top of Fiona's head appearing twice as big goes along with her literal "bigheaded" personality. Foil: While she and Leni are friends, Fiona is more confrontational and easily angered while Leni is a kind-heartedAll-Loving Hero. Girly Girl: She's a lot like Leni, being into fashion and clothes and other typically girly pursuits. Hair-Trigger Temper: Like Lori, Fiona is rather irritable and is easily angered by Lincoln and Clyde's antics in "Crimes of Fashion", and was quick to make rivals with Jackie and Mandee in "Everybody Loves Leni".

characters.name: Miguel
characters.description: Another close friend of Leni's who works alongside her and Fiona at Reininger's. Berserk Button: Anything to do with boxes in "Leader of the Rack". Camp Gay: He's got a high-pitched voice and enjoys fashion, and "Food Courting" outright confirms he likes men. Crush Blush: Miguel gets this in “Food Courting”. It’s shown that becomes really shy when it comes to his romantic situations, and naturally blushes because of it. Did Not Get The Guy: He does not end up with Gavin, as the latter had no interest in him and fell in love with Leni instead; despite that, he's cool with it and supports their relationship 100%.

characters.name: Jackie
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: She has tan skin and her voice actress would suggest she's Japanese or Asian. The Fashionista: She and Mandee seem to be this, constantly buying new clothes and having an opinion on people's fashion sense. It makes sense, considering she's a friend of Leni. Ink-Suit Actor: She resembles her voice actor in animated form. My God, What Have I Done?: She and the rest of Leni's friends all have a moment of this when they realise their feuding with each other caused Leni to miss out on a huge sale she was looking forward to, instead keeping herself at home all lonely and depressed. The friends take steps to rectify this, however. One-Steve Limit: She has the same name as one of the pageant girls mentioned above.

characters.name: Mandee
characters.description: The Fashionista: She and Jackie seem to be this, constantly buying new clothes and having an opinion on people's fashion sense. It makes sense, considering she's a friend of Leni. My God, What Have I Done?: She and the rest of Leni's friends all have a moment of this when they realise their feuding with each other caused Leni to miss out on a huge sale she was looking forward to, instead keeping herself at home all lonely and depressed. The friends take steps to rectify this, however. Satellite Character: She has only appeared whenever Jackie is around (not counting “Stage Plight” where only the latter was present). True Blue Femininity: Wears a blue shirt.

characters.name: Gavin
characters.description: Annoying Laugh: In "Force of Habits", he has a penchant of snorting while he laughs. Leni finds this his most annoying habit, though she soon gets over it. Amicable Exes: He's broken up with Leni by "Brawl of the Wild", but they remain friends. Nice Guy: Is definitely a sweet guy who is willing to help anyone, especially Leni. Official Couple: With Leni, until they broke up prior to the "Summer Camp" arc. Satellite Love Interest: In contrast to Bobby, Sam, and Benny, Gavin's character is entirely defined by being Leni's boyfriend.

characters.name: River
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: He tends to speak in a rather condescending, sarcastic manner. Leni even nicknames him Mr. Snarky in their first meeting. Fire-Forged Friends: He and Leni don't get along at first until they embark on a hike together and get stranded in the woods, in which they start getting along. Foil: He contrasts Leni in many ways in "Brawl of the Wild". Whereas Leni dresses fashionably, River dresses practically, such as having a vest with pockets to store food and wearing toed shoes for a tight grip. Official Couple: With Leni from "Brawl of the Wild" onwards. Soapbox Sadie: As mentioned in "Man of My Schemes" and seen in "Fruit Dispute", he frequently spends his time on protests.

characters.name: Sam Sharp
characters.description: A music-loving girl who is currently dating Luna. Alliterative Name:SamSharp. Annoying Younger Sibling: Her official bio reveals she has a brother named Simonnotewho is confirmed to be younger than Sam as of "Purrfect Gig", and according to her, Simon provides enough chaos for just one sibling. Ascended Extra: After just appearing as a background character, Sam finally got to have a plot with Luna in the episode "Racing Hearts". Big Sister Instinct: Zig-zagged in "Purrfect Gig". At first, it seems Sam is quite close to Simon that she's greatly concerned about his well-being at all times (like when she calls out Luna for suggesting to leave him outside Clyde's house alone all night). Later in the episode, however, she outright forgets about him and accidentally leaves him at Clyde's house. That said, she immediately rushes back upon realizing she left him behind before she and Luna then try to get him out of the house before theMcBrides catch him.

characters.name: Moon Goats
characters.description: Ascended Extra: They were initially unnamed minor characters, with Sully's primary purpose being to serve as aRed Herring, before getting bigger roles and characterization. Ambiguously Jewish: Mazzy’s name means “pearl” in Hebrew. Eyes Out of Sight: Mazzy's bangs obscure her eyes, much like Mick Swagger's. Kiddie Kid: Sully is definitely this in "Child's Play", as he's quite ditzy and has fond memories of playing a kazoo as a kid to the point of purchasing one from a toy store. This inspires the others to deliberately embrace their inner toddlers and play on the swings and a bounce house as inspiration for their songs. Know When to Fold 'Em: Inverted. In "Deep Cuts", the Music Club challenges the Sports Club to a fight, despite the fact that the rival club has over twice as many people, most of them are athletic and/or males, and one of them is a Karate bruiser. Needless to say, they looked rather outmatched. Fortunately, Lori crashes the golf kart and the fight is put to a stop before anyone can get hurt.

characters.name: Tabby
characters.description: A friend of Luna that she set up as a date for Lincoln. She eventually bonds with Liam, however. Anime Hair: Spiky, with a large tuft of it pointing upwards. Childish Tooth Gap: Has a gaping hole in her teeth. Delinquent Hair: She has a purple streak which goes upwards. Her hair also looks similar to a skunk. Nice Girl: Is the only girl that seems legitimately upset at having to date Liam instead of Lincoln, at least at first.

characters.name: Simon Sharp
characters.description: Alliterative Name:SimonSharp. Annoying Younger Sibling: According to Sam's bio from the graphic novels, Simon provides a lot of chaos for just one sibling. Butt-Monkey: Downplayed, but he gets hit with some slapstick comedy near the end of "Purrfect Gig". Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Like his sister, Simon has blonde hair and is shown to be a happy and fun-loving kid. Informed Attribute: Sam's description of Simon from her bio in the graphic novels implies that he's bit of a troublemaker, though his appearance in "Purrfect Gig" shows him to be friendly and well-mannered, and the only trouble he causes is indirect on his part.

characters.name: Nina
characters.description: Always Someone Better: Luna believes Nina is this to her after seeing how amazing she is with her guitar, thus resulting in her trying to prevent the Moon Goats from hiring her once Luan plants the idea in her head that she may become her permanent replacement. Though her bandmates insist that while Nina is brilliant, Luna is just as great herself. Animal Motifs: Ducks. Luna finds her playing a duck-shaped guitar for ducks down at the duck pond. Composite Character: She seems to be a mix of some of the main tomboy characters from the show. She's a punk rock chick who loves shredding on her guitar, similar to Luna. She also has a similar ethnicity and color scheme in her wardrobe to Ronnie Anne, as well as a shared talent for skateboarding. She also has a strong, tender relationship with animals, similar to Lana. The Rock Star: Similar to Luna, hence why she's the perfect replacement for her after Luna injures her hands in "Music to My Fears". Tomboy with a Girly Streak: She's a rocker girl like Luna who enjoys shredding on her guitar, and she's also very good with a skateboard. That said, she does wear a fair amount ofpinkand also has a soft, nurturing relationship with animals.

characters.name: Benjamin "Benny" Stein
characters.description: A boy interested in comedy and theatre, and Luan's love interest. Ambiguously Jewish: His full name is Benjamin Stein, thus sharing his name with Jewish actor and writerBen Stein. Ascended Extra: Benny was portrayed as merely one of many expendable one-shot love interests back in "L is for Love", most of which were never seen again. Come the end of season three, however, and suddenly this guy has a recurring role in the show, just like Sam. The Bus Came Back: Has a major role with Luan in "Stage Plight". The Big Damn Kiss: He shares one with Luan as part of theRomeo and Julietplay recital, having sharedhis first onewith her.

characters.name: The Drama Club
characters.description: Luan's friends from the Royal Woods High School'sDrama Club, which also includes herself and Benny. Other members include Shannon, Amy, Rex, Lyberti, Ruby, Spencer, among others.... Dork in a Sweater: Shannon, with her big round glasses and yellow turtleneck. Improv: "Director's Rut" shows they're all fond of inserting their own ideas into plays when one of them (Luan) gets director duty. Like Is, Like, a Comma: Ruby talks, like, like this. Official Couple: Amy and Rex are dating.

characters.name: Amy
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: She has one in "An Inspector Falls",as the main antagonist who sabatoges the show so she can get the lead role. Always Someone Better: Luan is this to her when it comes to solving mysteries and plotting. Clingy Jealous Girl: Amy usually has to keep Rex close because he doesn't trust him near any other girl. Driven by Envy:Amy plots to get the lead role of Agatha Mystery in the school play after it is revealed that Luan is chosen for the part instead of her. Girly Girl with a Tomboy Streak: Amy is a passionate theatre lover, and is quite romantic with her boyfriend, Rex, she gushes when she gets a love note, and she wears purple nail polish. She also wearspink shoes and a pink handbag, and is also into tap dancing. She seems fairly feminine overall, though she does wear pants and is also fairly outspoken, boisterous and confrontational in nature.

characters.name: Giggles
characters.description: A friend of Luan that she set up as a date for Lincoln. She, however, seems to become close to Zach. Big Beautiful Woman: She's rather chubby, but is rather cute as well. Cartoon Juggling: Juggles muffins during her date with Lincoln. Gag Nose: A red clown nose. The Hyena: She's nowhere near as bad as Luan, but she laughs a lot.

characters.name: Margo Roberts
characters.description: Lynn Jr.'s best friend and fellow sports player. Always Second Best: Naturally, with Lynn always having to be "number one" in everything, Margo is prone to being number 2 or 3 in any sports team she's in. Always Someone Better: Eventually she's able to do something impressive enough to eclipse Lynn's popularity during a soccer game in "Hero Today, Gone Tomorrow". Ascended Extra: After having multiple (mostly voiceless) cameos in seasons 2 and 3, she finally hasA Day in the Limelightin "Hero Today, Gone Tomorrow". Heterosexual Life-Partners: She's the closest friend Lynn has been shown to have in the series.

characters.name: Paula Price
characters.description: Alliterative Name:PaulaPrice. Artistic License – Sports: No sane coach or referee would allow her to play with that cast on, much less with a crutch. It's illegal and possibly even criminal to do so. She also occasionally uses her crutch in her plays, which counts as cheating. Ascended Extra: She was just one of Lynn's teammates in "Net Gains", but managed to snag a decent-sized role later in "Hero Today, Gone Tomorrow" and became one of Lynn's recurring friends ever since, frequently showing up alongside Margo and Maddie. Dark Horse Victory: She ends up scoring the winning goal at the end of "Hero Today, Gone Tomorrow", resulting in her overshadowing both Lynn and Margo (who were insisting that the other scored instead) in the eyes of fans. Determinator: Considering all the effort one would have to go through to move around in her condition (let alone during a sports event), she's this by default.

characters.name: Royal Woods Roller Queens
characters.description: Lynn's roller derby teammates besides herself and Margo. Other members include Maddie, Lainey and Nadia. Ascended Extra: Maddie was at first just part of Lynn and her roller derby team. But in season five, she has started hanging out with her more often, going to Dairyland with her and even joining her football team. The Glomp: Whenever Maddie and her boyfriend, Kaito, win an arcade game round, they like to celebrate their win by having a “victory hug,” which involves giving each other a tight, loving squeeze. Lesbian Jock: Lainey is one, being a roller derby player in a relationship with another girl named Alice. Masculine–Feminine Gay Couple: Lainey with her girlfriend, Alice. Downplayed, as Lainey is shown to be feminine along with Alice, as each wear a skirt and dress, use makeup, and partake in giggly flirting. However, Lainey is aLesbian Jock.

characters.name: The Royal Woods Turkey Jerkies
characters.description: Passionate Sports Girl: These girls are keen and enthusiastic to play basketball despite all the handicaps they have that limit their success in the game. Ragtag Bunch of Misfits: All of them have flaws that prevent them from being a great team. Amy is distracted by her phone, Maya often falls asleep at the worst time, Diane has sweaty palms, and Paula is crippled. But through the efforts of Lynn (and later Megan and Morgan), the team manages to make it much further into the competition than they would have otherwise.

characters.name: Polly Pain
characters.description: A friend of Lynn that she set up as a date for Lincoln. Turns out she has more in common with Rusty though. Alliterative Name:PollyPain. Ass Kicks You: Slams Lincoln with her booty, a move she likes to call "booty block". The Big Guy: The tallest of Lincoln's dates, and also the one who gets the most physical with him. The Bus Came Back: The second of Lincoln's dates to reappear after Haiku; she appears (or at least a girl who looks like her) in "Spell It Out" as part of Lynn's rowboat team, thoughshe doesn't speak.

characters.name: Dexter
characters.description: Brains and Brawn: The brains to Lynn's brawn, given they're a nerd and a jock, respectively. Bully and Wimp Pairing: Lynn can exhibit mild bullying tendencies at times (mainly with her siblings) and is certainly the part physically, being a really strong and tough girl. Dexter is a typical clutsy nerd with poor co-ordination skills. The two date for a while, until they break-up because they were only doing it for other reasons. Just Friends: He and Lynn decide to break-up but remain on relatively friendly terms with each other. Masculine Girl, Feminine Boy: Considering he's a little nerd kid datingLynn, this is a given. Unaffected by Spice: He is the only one of Lynn's prospective boyfriends to withstand the spiciness of the "Fire in the Belly" burger, which results in Lynn choosing him.

characters.name: Francisco
characters.description: Big Ol' Eyebrows: He has incredibly bushy eyebrows. Birds of a Feather: He loves sports, just likeLynn. Derailing Love Interests: In "Singled Out", Lynn claims she thought she had a crush on him, but was simply dehydrated. Phenotype Stereotype: Name's Francisco, has brown skin and raven hair. Satellite Love Interest: Basically exists to be Lynn's love interest in "L is for Love".

characters.name: Jenna
characters.description: All-Cheering All the Time: How she acts in "The Hurt Lockers" alongside her cheerleading crew, much to the dismay of her locker partner Liam. Foil: To Dodge from The Casagrandes. Both of them are the leaders of a rival team to the main characters (Ronnie Anne to Dodge, and Lynn Jr. to Jenna), who make a bet to get a particular spot somewhere (for Ronnie Anne and friends is the gym, and for Lynn and her friends is the bus). But while Dodge and her team wererelentless bullieswho kept antagonizing Ronnie Anne and her friends until they were defeated, Jenna and her squad manage to beat Lynn and her team at the cheer-off, comes up with a compromise so that they all get to ride the bus together, and they end up the episode on good terms with each other. Hero Antagonist: Despite how she and her squad arguably being the main antagonists of Cheer Pressure, they're actually the ones in the right for getting mad at Lynn and her teammates for disrespecting their sport. Take a Third Option: She's the one who comes up with a compromise so that Lynn and her friends can ride the bus with them. Tomboy and Girly Girl: She and her fellow cheerleaders are obviously the girly girls to Lynn, Margo, and Paula's tomboys.

characters.name: Henrik
characters.description: Always Second Best: He's been constantly beaten out by another boy named Hans at the Snow Fury. When he competes in "Alpining Away", he ends up getting beaten by Lynn instead (under the alias of Helga), although once he finds out the truth he sees that as another reason to like her because she challenges him to be a better athlete. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: He has dirty blond hair and is definitely a nice guy to be around. Love Interest: Henrik is notable for being Lynn's first genuine love interest. Signature Laugh: He yodels when he laughs. Not that it makes him any less cute to Lynn.

characters.name: Zia
characters.description: The Ace: She's as gifted at sports as Lynn is, thanks to her parents putting her in "every sports camp known to man". Canon Foreigner: Only exists inThe Really Loud House. Foil: To Lynn, being absolutely skilled at nearly every sport known to man. The difference is, Zia is slightlymore girlyand is more humble about her skill at sports. Gender-Blender Name:Assumingshe's of Indian descent like her actress. In South Asia (India, but especially Pakistan and Bangladesh), "Zia" is a boy's name. The Nicknamer: Frequently refers to Lincoln as "Spaghetti Arms" or "Spaghetti Legs".

characters.name: Haiku
characters.description: She's also part of the Morticians' Club, being the closest thing Lucy has to a best friend. Ascended Extra: She's the only one of the four girls who dated Lincoln in "Dance, Dance Resolution" who's become a highly recurring character, in contrast to the other three who turned out to just be one-shots. Boy Meets Ghoul: Apparently has a crush on a vampire. The Bus Came Back: The first of the four dates to reappear after "Dance, Dance Resolution" in "Out of the Picture" as part of the Mortician's Club with Lucy. In "The Write Stuff," Haiku appears as part of the poetry club. Cheated Angle: Herside-swept bangsare always covering the eye closest to the camera, no matter what direction she faces. However starting with "The Write Stuff", the bangs cover the farthest eye on occasion.

characters.name: The Morticians Club
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Downplayed, but in their first appearance in Season 2, they were extras who acted as one of many clubs that Lincoln and Clyde were trying to get into for a school yearbook photo. They wouldn't appear again until season 3, and even then it was only for a few seconds to act as Lucy's backup in two episodes. Starting with season 4 however, the club would gain increased focus as Lucy's own supporting characters in her spotlight episodes. Indeed, since "A Grave Mistake" the Morticians Club has played a central role as Lucy's friend group in every episode that she is a protagonist in. The Bus Came Back: In the episode "A Grave Mistake", Bertrand had to temporarily leave the Morticians Club, due to his family having a job on a cruise ship. He was absent in season 5, but later returned in season 6. Creepy Mortician: They started a club to practice the art of undertaking, and all share a love of the macabre. "Darkness von Gothick" Name: Some are named afterClassical Mythologyfigures (Morpheus, Persephone), others after real people (Dante,Boris,Bertrand), but they all fit this, including Lucy and Haiku. Nice, Mean, and In-Between: They are split between this half and half:Nice: Boris and Dante. The former is the more childish member with the highest sense of humor, while the latter has an equal amount of slapstick and still likes some things that are non-goth.Mean: Bertrand and Morpheus. Both are the most serious, with Bertrand as the former president who dislikes anything cutesy and Morpheus having the least sense of humor.In-between: Haiku and Persephone: The first acts as the second-in-command and the voice of reason to Lucy's actions, while the second isThe Quiet Onewho plays no major part in any episodes and has the least amount of presence unless the scene calls for it.

characters.name: Rocky Spokes
characters.description: Rusty's younger brother, and Lucy's love interest. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: After his debut in "Back in Black", he's never seen again despite being built up as Lucy's potential crush. Later in "L is for Love", Lucy is seen crushing on another boy, Silas, and Rocky is not brought up again. This is especially jarring as his brother Rusty has been featured more prominently as the seasons have progressed, and even their father has made a few minor appearances, but Rocky still hasn't been seen or even mentioned since season twonotewith the exception of a couple of mentioned in outside media - a Q&A Livestream in 2017 and a seemingly unused voice line inNickelodeon All-Star Brawl. He's not even mentioned when Rusty is listing off family members in '"How The Best was Won". Foil: To his brother, Rusty. Despite all his efforts to be considered a cool, popularladies man, Rusty is ultimately part of Lincoln's gang of geeky friends. Meanwhile, Rocky is a (mostly) normal, cool and laid back kid who has typical interests for a boy his age like playing sports. In his earlier appearances, Rusty was shown to be hanging out with other kids, but he ended up having only Lincoln, Clyde, Zach and Liam (and later Stella) as his only friends. Additionally,Rusty is a bit of an excitable wuss, beingAfraid of Blood,while Rocky shares Lucy's interest in blood, horror and the macabre. Hidden Depths: He seems like a average, normal kid at first, but he shares Lucy's interest in the macabre. Horrifying the Horror: A light-hearted and non-villainous example. Lucy can be quite scary at times given her dark and gothic nature, and she is frequently shown to be capable of frightening everyone she meets by suddenly speaking to them from behind when they didn't even know she was there. In "Back in Black", Rocky eventually manages to pull off the same thing on her.

characters.name: Silas
characters.description: A boy Lucy has a crush on in "L is for Love". Birds of a Feather: He is a gloomy goth, just like Lucy. Dub Name Change: His name is Samuel in the Polish dub. Exhausted Eye Bags: He has some bags under his eyes. Flat Character:Outside of being Lucy's love interest in "L is for Love",and being aGothlike her, he doesn't really have too many personality traits.

characters.name: Lana's Friends
characters.description: Eyes Out of Sight: Two of Lana's friends have hair that covers their eyes. Lady Looks Like a Dude: The friend who talks (and tells Lana she's not allowed at their mud pit) has a very tomboyish look, though the longer hair, visible eyelashes and bright magenta shoes just about give away her gender. The Bus Came Back: After seemingly being forgotten about and unseen after "Cover Girls", the other two with bangs made a brief return in "Fool Me Twice". The Pig-Pen: All of them love playing in mud just as much as Lana herself. The Voiceless: Neither of the kids with bangs ever says a word in any of the cameo appearances they make.

characters.name: Skippy
characters.description: A boy Lana has a crush on in "L is for Love". Birds of a Feather:He enjoys fixing things, just like Lana. The Bus Came Back: He returns in the comic story "Skip to the End" fromSister Resister, which came out about six years after "L is for Love" aired. Distaff Counterpart: Basically a male version of Lana in that both are professional mechanics who wear backwards baseball caps. Mr. Fixit: Like Lana, he enjoys fixing bikes.

characters.name: Winston
characters.description: Lola's crush from "L is for Love". He is a posh boy. Birds of a Feather: He is interested in beauty pageants, just like Lola. Hold Up Your Score: Lola remembers Winston holding up a "10" card during one of her pageants. She later tries to impress him by holding up a "10" after he falls on his face while doing down a slide. Goofy Print Underwear: "Wild Goss Chase" reveals he wears Blarney underpants. Improbable Age: Despite him being a little kid, he's a member of the jury during one of Lola's pageants.

characters.name: Lindsay Sweetwater
characters.description: Lola's biggest pageant rival. Adaptation Dye-Job: In her first physical appearance in "Fool Me Twice", the colors of her body could not be determined since she was shown through a green screen.Loud and Proud, the sixth issue of thecomics, showed her with orange hair, but the main series later retconned this into her having red hair when she showed up in person in "Crown and Dirty". Always Second Best: Her reasoning behind getting dirt on Lola is that she always takes second place to Lola despite her efforts. Enemy Mine: Admits she doesn't like Lincoln (most likely because she beat him earlier in a pageant as seen in "Making the Case"), but is willing to help him just to get revenge on Lola. The Ghost: Initially, due toonly her eyes being visiblein the closet she was in.

characters.name: Jackie, Claudette, and Chinah
characters.description: A trio of girls who regularly compete in beauty pageants like Lola Loud, but are much more experienced when it comes to the stuff like regional and national pageants. The Ace:Chinah has competed in both regional and national beauty pageants and, according to Jackie, holds the record for the most pageant titles won before the age of 7—Chinah's the one who's ultimately crowned "Little Miss Southeastern Michigan."Jackie, according to Chinah, regularly appears in toothpaste commercialsnoteJackie shows off her pearly whites when Chinah says thisand, during rehearsals for the pageant, is revealed to be a skilled gymnast—she's the first runner-up (2nd-place) for the title of Little Miss Southeastern Michigan.Claudette's pageant skills are unknown, but, just like Chinah and Jackie, she's clearly much more experienced than Lola is when it comes to stuff like high(er)-level pageants—Claudette also appears to come from a wealthy family, as she claims that all of gowns (at least the ones she wears for pageants) are all custom-made in (and imported from) Paris, France. She ends up being the second runner-up (3rd-place) for the title of Little Miss Southeastern Michigan. Chinah has competed in both regional and national beauty pageants and, according to Jackie, holds the record for the most pageant titles won before the age of 7—Chinah's the one who's ultimately crowned "Little Miss Southeastern Michigan."
