characters.name: Meli Ramos
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Returns for the twins' seventh birthday party in "Strife of the Party". Latino Is Brown: Her last name is Ramos, and she has dark skin. Red Oni, Blue Oni: The blue to Lola's red. Meli wears dull grey clothes, is aShrinking Violet, is introverted and nervous and needs to seek out Lola for help to be more socially active. Lola is an excitable and emotional, bright pink wearing, outgoing girl who takes Meli under her wing to come out of her shell more. Shrinking Violet: She's very much this at first, so much so that she ended up receiving Lola's help to enable her to become more outgoing.

characters.name: Cricket Van Doren
characters.description: The Ace: Lola considers her to be this. Her introductory scene is Lola basically gushing over how much of an accomplished international pageant legend she is and listing some of her achievements. Always Someone Better: She's an international pageant legend who has won a crown on every continent. As opposed to Lola, Lindsay, and the other local Royal Woods girls who are small time in comparison. Even Jackie, Claudette, and Chinah are only regional/national level competitors (and they were already this trope in spades to Lola) while Cricket is international level. Girly Girl with a Tomboy Streak: She is a prim and proper pageant girl who is obviously very feminine in every regard, perhaps to an ever greater extent than Lola. She also enjoys cutting loose sometimes as being prim and proper constantly is hard work, and she finds the chaotic environment of the Loud House to actually be quite fun and appealing. She also shows a fondness towards Lana's hostile pet snake. Light Feminine and Dark Feminine: From what we've seen, Cricket is a sweetheart whose kindness probably rivals Leni's, while Lola is far more prone to aggression, manipulation, and fierce competitiveness. Both of them are very prim and proper pageant girls. Nice Girl: Despite being the most accomplished pageant girl seen in the show so far, she's actually easily one of the least snobbish or jerkish. She's completely friendly, polite, and welcoming towards Lola when they first meet and is even accepting of the brash and rough Loud siblings. Even when she finds out Lola has been lying to her, she forgives her fairly easily.

characters.name: Kayla, Ashley, and Kristen
characters.description: Pink Is Feminine: Kayla wears a pink sweater. Remember the New Guy?: They are introduced as new characters but the Loud family seems to have known them for a long time. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: With Lana's old friends absent, they seem to take their place as her friend group.

characters.name: Darcy Helmandollar
characters.description: One of Lisa's classmates whom Lisa befriends in "Friend or Faux?" to get an A for social skills on her report card. The two later become genuine friends. Ambiguously Brown: She has dark skin, but her exact ethnicity is unknown. Big Eater: In "InTODDnito", she manages to eat a large amount cake for her small frame, much to Todd's surprise. Big Guy, Little Guy: The Big Guy to Lisa's Little Guy. Downplayed, as Lisa is only two thirds Darcy's height. Birthday Episode: Turns 5 years old in "InTODDnito".

characters.name: David
characters.description: Acting Your Intellectual Age: Being aChild Prodigy, David behaves like an adult and subverts the typical behavior of his childish peers. Birds of a Feather: David is aChild Prodigywho loves science, just like Lisa, who has a crush on him. Child Prodigy: Like Lisa, he knows how to do chemistry and write. Distaff Counterpart: He could be seen as the male version of Lisa in that both areChild Prodigygeniuses who practice chemistry, areWise Beyond Their Years, and wearNerd Glasses. Labcoat of Science and Medicine: He's into science and wears a white lab coat.

characters.name: ChandlerMcCann
characters.description: One of the popular kids at Royal Woods Elementary and the closest thing Lincoln has to a personal nemesis. His dad works at a sewage plant. Ascended Extra: Chandler's appearances were actually very rare before Season 5, the season where he starts becoming a recurring annoyance in Lincoln's life. The Bully: Lincoln's personal heckler and bringer of misery. The Bus Came Back: After only a cameo in Season 2, he finally returns as a major character in "Jeers for Fears". Characterization Marches On: Started out as the most popular kid in school admired by everyone before evolving into aHated by Allbully as the show went on.

characters.name: Bratty Kid
characters.description: Evil Counterpart: Perhaps "evil" is a bit of a stretch, but he's notably aJerkasswho looks similar to Lincoln. Identical Stranger: He is meant to resemble Lincoln, despite the two having had little interaction. Jerkass: Laughs at Lincoln's expense, and later swipes the last box of Zombie Bran that Lincoln worked hard to get. Laser-Guided Karma: Gets one when he's taken out of the store by his mom after the havoc he wreaked while fighting with Lincoln. No Name Given: His real name is never revealed.

characters.name: Hank and Hawk
characters.description: Afraid of Blood: Hank and Hawk get nauseous when seeing Clyde’s nosebleed. This is later turned against them in Lucy's corn maze, where she pours a bucket of fake blood on them. Ambiguously Brown: Hank has darker skin, but he isn't black like Clyde. Ascended Extra: They play a minor role during their first appearance in "The Loudest Yard", and later become the main antagonists of "Tricked!" Big Dumb Bully: Hank and Hawk are the "big, muscular, not very bright" type of bullies. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: They're notevilper se, so it's more like Even Jerks Have Loved Ones. However, they seem to be best friends. Their bromance is so strong, they do everything together. Even if it includes barfing and passing out.

characters.name: Lacey St. Clair
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: She’s snobby and rude towards people whom she believes are lower class than her. Ambiguously Brown: She has a tanned skintone but her exact ethnicity is unknown. Foil: To Lola. Both are girly girls compared to Lana, and both have competitive natures relating to their fields of interest (pageants for Lola, fancy dog competitions for Lacey). But Lola genuinely loves her sister and has aheart of goldbehind all her negative behavioral traits. Lacey is malicious and doesn't really come across as so redeemable. Lola accepts Lana the way she is and even willingly hangs out with her (for the most part, as sometimes their clashing personalities can lead to conflict), while Lacey looks down on Lana and antagonizes forfor the fun of it. Girly Girl: Is possibly just as girly as Lola, if not moreso, given that Lola has a prominenttomboyish streak. Karma Houdini: Played with. She bullies Lana and then still wins the dog competition anyway due to Lana's forfeit after she changed Charles too much in the process. All she gets as comeuppance is getting mud splashed on her, but considering how much she hates mud, this may be more of a punishment for her than it seems.

characters.name: The Bus Bullies
characters.description: A trio of bullies on the school bus who antagonize Lincoln and his friends for sitting on the back seat. Big, Thin, Short Trio: Anderson is the relatively large, muscular boy in the group, Taylor is the tall and slender girl, and Pablo is the shorter geeky one. Conspiracy Theorist: Pablo has apparently believed Mr. Bolhofner is an alien for years. Disproportionate Retribution: The reasons for their antagonistic actions are pretty petty considering the reason they bully Lincoln and his friends is because the latter was sitting on their seat, which is located in the very back of the bus,and they weren't even aware that was the bullies' seat.Lincoln’s friends got targeted for inadvertently getting them dirty and being close to him. By the end of the school day, Lincoln assumed they ought to have cooled their heads, but nope, the pummelings continue for several days in a row. They don’t even quit when Lincoln and his friends stop going to the bus, insteadtaking it out on every other passenger because they’re pissed their targets weren’t around anymore. Evil Counterpart:Anderson to Byron: They're both big Middle Schoolers. But when it comes to relationships, Anderson lacks the "Friendship" part of Byron'sCool Kid-and-Loser Friendship's.Taylor to Ronnie Anne: They're both tough girls. But while Ronnie Anne chose tobecome a better person, Taylor didn't and still picks on other kids.Pablo to Bobby: TheNerdy Bullyto Bobby'sKind Hearted Simpleton. Pablo is a nerdy person who likes to intimidate others while Bobby on the other hand, is a Ditz who likes to help others when he can.

characters.name: Ryan Miller
characters.description: The son of the diabolical Miller family who work for S.U.S.P.E.N.S.E., an organisation that plots to destroy the world's cherries. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: The Miller family appear to be a perfectly nice, amicable, welcoming, andnormalfamily at first glance. It takes Lincoln and Clyde utilising their agent detective skills to figure out that all was not as it seemed with them. Does Not Like Spam:Exaggerated; Ryan hates cherries so much that he's willing to go along with his parents' plan to destroy all the cherries in Royal Woods. Evil Nerd: He appears rather geekish and is a member of an evil family and organisation that wants to destroy the cherries in Royal Woods and cripple the local economy. Of course, with him being a spy, the nerdy appearance could just be a part of his undercover routine. Evil Counterpart: Like Lincoln, Ryan is a fair-haired pre-teen boy who is the son of a couple that somewhat physically resembles a slightly younger version of Lynn Sr and Rita. However, while Lincoln is a good kid (selfish streak and other vices aside), Ryan is evil and devious.

characters.name: Maggie
characters.description: A typical emo girl. She celebrated her 13th birthday in the episode "Funny Business". 13 Is Unlucky: Lincoln's successful streak as a birthday clown came to an absolute halt the moment he came face-to-face with this angsty 13-year-old teenager. Eerie Pale-Skinned Brunette: It helps in selling her emo look. Oddly, her mom seems to beAmbiguously Brown. Emotionless Girl: Being emo, Maggie displays little emotion (sans smiling at Lincoln and Luan's mime act). Foil: To Luan. While both of them like pantomime, they are complete polar opposites. Luan is upbeat, cheerful, optimistic, and comedy-loving, while Maggie is emo, stoic, depressed, and hates having fun.

characters.name: Aidan
characters.description: Nice Guy: He seems like a nice, well-mannered and respectful boy from what little we see of him. Wise Beyond Their Years: Mostly in the sense that he speaks in a articulate and grammatically correct manner for a toddler.

characters.name: Billy
characters.description: Mistaken Identity: Lincoln and Clyde thought he was Lily. One-Shot Character: Unlike his dad, who's had several appearances, he only makes one appearance. Walking Shirtless Scene: Like Lily, he doesn't wear a shirt.

characters.name: TheMcCauleyKids
characters.description: Caleb and Camille, two young kids who don't take kindly to Lynn's rough methods of babysitting. The Bus Came Back: They return in the comic story "Find of the Century" in an imaginary scenario fromThe Struggle is Real, which came out about a year after "Sitting Bull" aired. Children Are Innocent: They're nice, mild-mannered, well-behaved, and do not enjoy the violent and roughhousing ways of Lynn Loud. Foil: To the Fox kids, obviously. The Fox Quintuplets are little hellraisers who love to roughhouse and be very naughty and mischevious. TheMcCauleysare far more behaved and good-natured, and don't like Lynn's rough ways of babysitting, unlike the Fox's who love it. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: Their pajama wear is quite similar looking, but Camille's is colored pink and Caleb's is colored blue.

characters.name: The Fox Quintuplets
characters.description: A family of four boys and one girl. Ascended Extra: One of the quintuplets, Pam, made a small appearance in "Breaking Dad". She and her brothers make a return in "Sitting Bull", where they're given a much bigger role and characterization. Babysitter's Nightmare: The four eldest Loud sisters, considered Royal Woods' best babysitters in most circumstances, have all suffered under them. Birthday Buddies: "Present Danger" reveals that they share their birthday with Lincoln. Birthday Episode: A downplayed example. "Present Danger", which is a straight example of this trope for Lincoln, establishes that the Fox quintuplets share the same birthday as him, as Gus holds a medieval-themed birthday party for them at a his restaurant (albeit off-screen).

characters.name: Beatrix Yates
characters.description: Brainy Brunette: She has dark hair and is very tech-savvy. Ink-Suit Actor: Beatrix resembles her voice actress, Stephanie Sheh. The Ugly Guy's Hot Daughter: She's pretty and largely contrasts with Bumper Sr. in regard to appearance.

characters.name: Belle Yates
characters.description: Identical Stranger: She bears a striking resemblance to a black version of Luan judged by her braces, socks, and ponytail. Pink Means Feminine: Her scarf and hairbow are both colored pink. Pubescent Braces: She wears braces.

characters.name: Bumper Yates Jr.
characters.description: Ancestral Name: He's named after his father, Bumper Sr.

characters.name: Beau Yates
characters.description: Child Prodigy: He is young, but is as intelligent as his siblings and is even fluent in Korean. Childish Tooth Gap: He has a gap in his teeth. Nerd Glasses: He wears glasses with rectangular frames.

characters.name: Howard and HaroldMcBride
characters.description: All Gays Love Theater: One of them (it's unclear which one since the Louds seem to be on aLast-Name Basiswith them) put himself in theater school by working as a plumber. They also have weekly theater nights in which Clyde is included. Alliterative Name:Howard andHarold. AlsoMr. andMr.McBride, which they're often called by the Louds. Breakout Character: They became more and more prominent as the series went on, thanks to their positive reception as a married gay couple. A Day in the Limelight: They have their first huge role in "Attention Deficit". They have another one in "Snow Way Down". Depending on the Artist: Howard has buck teeth, but depending on the scene, they either stick out or are hidden when he closes his mouth. The former is the most common.

characters.name: Nana GayleMcBride
characters.description: Cool Old Lady: Despite her age, she is still stable enough to join Lincoln and Clyde on a David Steele mission, and is a kickboxing expert. Unseen No More: Had several mentions in the first four seasons before finally appearing onscreen in "Resident Upheaval".

characters.name: Bud Grouse
characters.description: The Louds' grumpy neighbor. Ascended Extra: Going by the credits of his debut episode where he was referred as just "Neighbor", Grouse was apparently not meant to be anything more than just that. Completely different from his current status as one of the most prominent non-Loud characters, having multiple episodes dedicated to him (including the first 30-minute one of the whole series). Cranky Neighbor: The Louds' antics, especially Lincoln's, tend to get on his nerves. But deep down, he considers them friends. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Has a different design in his the first two episodes he appears in "Chore and Peace" and "A Novel Idea" before gaining his permanent one in "A Tattler's Tale". Freudian Excuse: The reason he's rude to the Louds (or possibly the reason he gets extra grumpy around Christmas) is because he himself comes from a big family but is unable to see them, so they remind him of his loved ones. Later episodes also indicate that his wife is deceased, so that's probably a factor as well.

characters.name: Bumper Sr. and Jancey Yates
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Bumper Sr. has dark skin but isn't black like Clyde. Gag Nose: They're both designed with pretty long noses. Good Parents: They raise their kids the best way they can and take them to plenty of different activities to make them "well-rounded". Fat and Skinny: Bumper Sr. is fat, Jancey is skinny. Happily Married: They are married and very much in love.

characters.name: Dr. Simmons
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: In Season 1, he first appeared in "The Blemish Dilemish" and never surfaced again for that season. He came back in the Season 2 premiere, "A Musical to Remember". Canon Foreigner: So far only exists inThe Really Loud House. The Medic: Being a family doctor and all. Trademark Favorite Food: He has a fondness for fried chicken, which Lynn Sr. exploits in "The Blemish Dilemish" to get him to be the Louds' family doctor.

characters.name: Rodney Spokes
characters.description: Neat Freak: He has a habit of wanting his clothes for sale to be in one piece. Official Couple: Has this with Katherine Mulligan of all people. Older Than They Look: While nothing really calls attention to it, he easily looks more like he could be Rusty's older brother than his father. Parents as People: While he does care for Rusty, he doesn't always give the best advice to his son about how to attract females. He also unintentionally puts pressure on Rusty in taking care of the family business. Moreover, Rusty has a habit in makingcertain things about himself, suggesting that while Rodney is a loving parent, he hasn't done the best job in teaching Rusty on how to treat others the way he wants to be treated. Strong Family Resemblance: He looks like an older version of his sons.

characters.name: Mr. & Mrs. Gurdle
characters.description: Conspiracy Theorist: As if theirtinfoil hatsdidn't make it obvious enough. They're always looking for potential anomalies that they allege are hidden in plain sight. Fat and Skinny: Mr. Gurdle is the "Fat" to his wife's "Skinny". Mr. Gurdle is chubby while Mrs. Gurdle has a slim build. No Full Name Given: Their first names have yet to be revealed. Parents as People: Mr. & Mrs. Gurdle do care for their son Zach. However, they are also incredibly flawed as parents to say the least as the two have a habit of dragging him into crazy alien hunts, even when it may interfere with his day plans as shown in "No Bus No Fuss" and "Broadcast Blues". Also, since Zach'sConspiracy Theoristtends to annoy other kids, this implies that despite the two being genuinely caring and loving parents, they haven't done the best job in teaching their son proper social skills. Strong Family Resemblance: Mr. Gurdle is pretty much an older, overweight version of his son.

characters.name: Mimi Hunnicut
characters.description: Beehive Hairdo: Though the episode "Hunn-cut Gems" reveals that it's actually a wig. Older Than They Look: You'd be forgiven for thinking she's Liam's mother and not hisgrandmother. Parents as People: More like “Grandparents as People”. She’s close with her grandson Liam and generally a loving grandmother, but sometimes she ends up being too strict with him when he tries to have fun and she also has a habit of struggling to separate her farm mindset from her citizen mindset. Said mindset also seems to have been passed onto Liam as well which causes Liam to act somewhat eccentric towards his peers. This implies that despite being a loving and caring grandparent, she hasn’t done the best job in teaching Liam how to separate his own farm mindset from his own citizen mindset. Southern Belle: She's (usually) friendly and speaks with a Southern accent. Unseen No More: After mentions throughout the first three seasons, she appears onscreen for the first time in "Stall Monitor" of Season 4.

characters.name: Agnes Johnson
characters.description: A fifth-grade teacher. She's taught Lincoln and his friends from Seasons 1 to 4. Altering the Grades: Downplayed in "Project Loud House", where Mrs. Johnson changes the grade on Lincoln's assignment, where he has his sisters pose as a diorama, from an A to an A- becauseLuandrenched her with water. Demoted to Extra: She loses prominence from Season 5 onward with Lincoln moving to middle school. So far, she's had a few cameo appearances since then. Hidden Depths:Or not so hidden. Mrs. Johnson likes mechanical bull riding.She accidentally showed the class a picture of her doing so in "Shell Shocked".It's the stated explanation for how she broke her leg in "Study Muffin". Or not so hidden. Mrs. Johnson likes mechanical bull riding.

characters.name: Principal Wilbur T. Huggins
characters.description: The principal of Royal Woods Elementary. Animals Hate Him: "Sand Hassles" and "She's All Bat" have him get attacked by crows and bats, respectively. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: A work colleague case with him and Cheryl Farrell. He's a sullenDean Bittermanand Cheryl is aBig FunNice Girl Dean Bitterman: He can easily come across as this on the surface. Less so if you learn hisHidden Depths. Demoted to Extra: Downplayed. With Lincoln and his friends graduating from Royal Woods Elementary, Principal Huggins is not around as much anymore, but he still occasionally appears in Lucy and the twins' episodes.

characters.name: Coach Pacowski
characters.description: The gym teacher at Royal Woods Elementary. Acrofatic: He is surprisingly agile for a man of his physique. Basement Dweller: He lives with his mother in a houseboat. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: He's the brooding boy (With him being aDrill Sergeant Nastygym teacher) to Nurse Patti's gentle girl (With her being akindly nurse) Demoted to Extra: Like with the other teachers, as Lincoln and his friends graduated from Elementary School, Coach Pacowski is not around as much. He seems to have it worse than Mrs. Johnson and Principal Huggins, however, as he wascompletely absent from Season 5's "For Sale By Loner" to Season 8's "The Winning Spirit".

characters.name: Nurse Patti
characters.description: The school nurse at Royal Woods Elementary. Ambiguously Brown: She has a dark skin tone, but she's not exactly black. Hidden Depths: She enjoys playing mini-golf. Hypocritical Humor: In "Hobblin' the Goblin", she attempts to eat a cupcake just after saying she's giving a lecture to first graders on healthy eating. Morality Pet:To Coach Pacowski.

characters.name: Ms. Shrinivas
characters.description: But Not Too Foreign: Her last name implies that she may be Indian. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: With Lisa aging up andgraduatingfrom kindergarten, she hasn't made an appearance since. Despite still working at the same school Lisa goes to. Surrounded by Idiots: Inverted. Her students are of the average kindergartner intelligence, which she can handle; it's Lisa's heightened intelligence, unchildlike behavior, and overall antics that prove to be challenging. Tuckerization: Named after former writer Sheela Shrinivas.

characters.name: Ms. Allegra
characters.description: A first-grade teacher. She's taught Lana and Lola from Seasons 1-4, and Lisa from Season 5 onwards. Let's See YOU Do Better!: After being fed up with Lisa's “corrections”, she makes Lisa try to teach the class herself. Noodle Incident: She claims that before Lisa, Lola was the worst Loud she's had to deal with in her career. Knowing Lola'sBratty Half-Pintnature, whatever Lola's done under Miss Allegra's tutelage definitely was not pretty, and it's implied the twins weren't the first Louds she's dealt with.

characters.name: Cheryl Farrell
characters.description: Beehive Hairdo:Lampshadedin "Double Trouble", where she claims a horde of bees chasing her are mistaking her beehive for theirs. Big Eater: In "Brave the Last Dance", Clyde presents free sample desserts. Cheryl takes three of them. Big Fun: She's a plump woman with a very upbeat and kind-hearted attitude. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: A work colleague case with her and Principal Huggins. She's aBig FunNice Girland Huggins is a sullenDean Bitterman. Dreadful Musician: "Listen Out Loud" reveals she's a terrible singer. When put on the spot to sing by Lana, Cheryl lets loose with a terrible rendition of "Hush Little Baby".

characters.name: Mr. Bolhofner
characters.description: A math teacher at Royal Woods Middle School, and Lincoln's homeroom teacher from Season 5 onwards. Ambiguously Brown: Mr. Bolhofner has very dark skin, but nothing else to suggest a specific ethnicity. Ascended Extra: Went from a minor character as Lynn's teacher to a major supporting character as Lincoln's teacher. Butt-Monkey:Not as prominent as Lincoln or Lenibut he has suffered his own mishaps with good examples being blocked in the car park by Rita, getting tackled by Zach because the latter thought he was possessed by an alien, being asked anInnocently Insensitivequestion courtesy of Stella, having his car totaled by Leni and falling into a sinkhole. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: A work colleague example with him and Mrs. Salter with him being a grouchySadist Teacher(Albeit sometimesnice) and Mrs. Salter being one of the nicer teachers at Royal Woods Middle School.

characters.name: Mrs. Salter
characters.description: Nice Girl: One of the nicer teachers at Royal Woods Middle School.

characters.name: Meryl Farrell
characters.description: Beehive Hairdo: Just like Cheryl. Big Fun: Like her twin sister, she's a plump woman with a very upbeat and kind-hearted attitude. Foil: Cheryl and Meryl look pretty much identical to each other, but they differ greatly in personality:Cheryl seems like the more intelligent one and is generally more mature and responsible.Meryl, while not stupid, is a bit more feeble-minded than her sister and is also generally a bit more reckless. Cheryl seems like the more intelligent one and is generally more mature and responsible. Meryl, while not stupid, is a bit more feeble-minded than her sister and is also generally a bit more reckless.

characters.name: Chef Pat
characters.description: Berserk Button: Flip trying to steal her food or drinks, which usually warrants her chasing him away with a shrill shout of "PHILLIPINI!!!!" Early Installment Character-Design Difference: She had more stains on her shirt and apron and visible teeth sticking out in "Kernel of Truth" and "Saved By the Spell". Gonk: Her appearance can best be described as "trollish". Jerk with a Heart of Gold: "Diss the Cook" shows that she's been subjecting the Loud kids to terrible lunches because Rita supposedly didn't invite her to the high school graduation party. However, when she learns that it was a misunderstanding, sheexpresses genuine remorseandtries to make amends for it. Lethal Chef: "Kernel of Truth" shows that one of the ingredients in her one-bean chili is a boot. However, "Diss the Cook" shows that she's capable of being aSupreme Chef, though she would often invoke this trope on the Louds out of spite.

characters.name: Principal Ramirez
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: She is completely and utterly useless in solving Lincoln's middle school issues, even contributing to them by transferring him to a Canadian school. Karma Houdini: She gets no punishments in "Too Cool for School" for endangering her students aside from getting called out by Astrid. Ms. Fanservice: You can tell by the running outfit she wore in “Too Cool for School”. No Sympathy: She sometimes has no empathy about the gang’s misfortunes. Nice, Mean, and In-Between: The stern but forgiving In Between to Huggins’ Mean and Rivers’ Nice.

characters.name: Principal Rivers
characters.description: The Ditherer: Of "The Wishy-Washy" type with shades of "The Insecure/Submissive". She's too spineless to actually assert her authority and just can't seem to make up her mind about anything. The pressure of trying to decide which school club to cut drives her to lie on the floor in theTroubled Fetal Position. Nice Girl: Despite her tendency to be a ditherer, she's usually abenevolent principal. Nice, Mean, and In-Between: The timid but calm Nice to Huggins’ Mean and Ramirez’s In Between.

characters.name: Oliver
characters.description: Hyper-Competent Sidekick: Rivers isn't by any means an idiot but she has such a tendency to be adithererthat he ends up having to make decisions for her.

characters.name: Kate Bernardo
characters.description: The drama teacher at Royal Woods High School. Ambiguous Situation:She may be married, since she goes by the title Mrs., though her husband is never seen.In "Prom-Com" she mentions having a first husband, though it's unclear whether he died or they got divorced, or how many times she's been married. She may be married, since she goes by the title Mrs., though her husband is never seen. In "Prom-Com" she mentions having a first husband, though it's unclear whether he died or they got divorced, or how many times she's been married. Ascended Extra: She was originally just Bobby's drama teacher that was called up for a prank in "Jeers for Fears", but from "Stage Plight" onwards, she more or less becomes Luan's mentor and a recurring character for any situation whenever a plot calls for it in several episodes during the Rubiner era.

characters.name: Police Officer
characters.description: A policeman of Royal Woods. Ambiguous Situation: Are the Loud family being confronted by different cops, or are they confronted by the same one (albeit with a slight redesign and different voices) at times? Cool Shades: He wears sunglasses and upholds the law. Fat Bastard: Played with and subverted. He has a gut but despite his disapproval of the Louds causing a public disturbance, he does cooperate well with them. No Name Given: His name is never mentioned, and he is simply credited as "Police Officer".

characters.name: Officer Schoffner
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: After being absent since "Rita Her Rights", she returns physically in "Close Encounters of the Nerd Kind". One of the Kids: She's a stern cop but "Close Encounters of the Nerd Kind" show she's willing to dress up for Halloween. Reasonable Authority Figure: She arrested Rita for seemingly committing a streak of crimes but upon seeing how often the latter's kids and husband need her, she sympathetically lets her go.

characters.name: Officer Shirley
characters.description: A police officer who is called by Rita when the latter tries to report a supposed burglar. All There in the Script: Her name is only revealed in the credits. Ambiguously Brown: Shirely's ethnicity isn't really clear but her medium dark skin tone and her voice actor being black seems to imply she may have some black heritage in her. Police Are Useless: A basically justified case. A very tired Rita tries to explain to her that an alleged thief (later revealed to be Mrs. Bernardo in disguise) robbing Jean-Juan's but due to Rita's exhausted state and tone, Shirley believes that Rita is probably just hallucinating the scenario.

characters.name: Phillip "Flip" Phillipini
characters.description: The owner of Flip's Food & Fuel, a gas station and convenience store. Alliterative Name:Phillip "Flip"Phillipini. Ambiguously Human: "Blinded By Science" reveals that while he looks human on the outside, he's not exactly human on the inside. He's got organs in the wrong spots and can't feel pain at times, not to mention he's able to withstand subzero temperatures. In "Any Given Sundae", he's established to have already grown asecondset of wisdom teeth, and as a teenager, he was able to spontaneously grow his mustache in anger. Also, according to "Flip This Flip", hesweats nacho cheese. Ascended Extra: Flip's way more prominent in later seasons, enough to be considered aSpotlight-Stealing Squadfor some. Buy or Get Lost: In the short "Muscle Fish", he's stated to have once kicked out a kid for loiteringwhile his mom was checking out.

characters.name: Chester "Chunk" Monk
characters.description: Luna's friend and roadie. Badasses Wear Bandanas: In his first appearance, he wears one. Bouncer: Served as one at one of Luna's sleepovers. A Day in the Limelight: Along with Luna, he's the main focus of "Roadie To Nowhere". Eccentric Mentor: Chunk seems to fancy himself one. He has a touched look of pride when Luna performs at the Royal Rumble which he himself performed at when he was a kid.

characters.name: Scoots
characters.description: Age-Gap Romance: In "The Boss Maybe", she has one with a younger, buff man. Ascended Extra: Given that she only appeared in one episode in Season One, she more than likely was intended to be nothing more than a one-shot gag character. Cool Car: well, cool scooter. It's capable of freeway speeds and apparently has aHammerspaceseat and helmet compartment. Cool Old Lady: She is mostly agrumpy old woman, but she has her moments, like in "Mall of Duty", where she helps Lincoln rescue Lily from a runaway train. She is also a fan of survivalist Rip Hardcore and calls him her Bae.In "Pulp Friction", Lincoln apparently thinks of her as both cool enough and mean enough to be a super villain in his own comic book. In "Pulp Friction", Lincoln apparently thinks of her as both cool enough and mean enough to be a super villain in his own comic book.

characters.name: Kotaro
characters.description: Lynn Sr.'s best friend. Nice Guy: He seems to be a pretty decent fellow. Recurring Extra: Usually shows up with a minor role whenever the story needs showing one of Lynn Sr.'s friends. Appears a little more frequently once he starts working at Lynn's Table. Satellite Character: Generally, not much is known of him other than the fact that he's a close friend of Lynn Sr.'s, and that both share a lot of the same interests (i.e. vans, music, cow bells, etc).

characters.name: Grant
characters.description: Ascended Extra: He was a nameless fast food employee, but now works directly under the Louds. Burger Fool: He certainly thinks of his job at the Burpin' Burger as this."I can't take another second in this greasy dungeon!" Casting Gag:He's voiced by Grant Palmer, who voiced Lincoln from "Left in the Dark" to "A Fair to Remember" before hitting puberty.

characters.name: Mrs. Carmichael
characters.description: Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Downplayed. She has someMean Bosshabits and accusing Leni of stealing was a little unfair but she's a nice and friendly woman for the most part. Mean Boss: Downplayed. Mrs. Carmichael can be a reasonable manager, but she's shown to be very demanding, and enforces certain questionable policies like prohibiting Reininger's workers fromshopping for clothes at rival stores. She also fires Leni over circumstantial evidence instead of any sort of concrete proof in "Crimes of Fashion". Not So Above It All: The only reason she doesn't fire Fiona from violating the aforementioned store policy is because the deal for the dress Fiona bought wasthatgood.

characters.name: Dana Dufresne
characters.description: A male-to-female transgender beauty pageant host and judge. Alliterative Name:DanaDufresne. Effeminate Voice: Even before transitioning, Dana had quite a feminine and flamboyant voice. Gag Nose: Pre-transition, her nose was quite long. It's shortened a bit post-transition, though it's still larger than most characters. Large Ham: Being a pageant host, she's quite the flamboyant type.

characters.name: Tyler
characters.description: Age-Gap Romance: He has one with Scoots. Dumb Jock: He is not bright as he writes a number upside down. Top-Heavy Guy: Note his appearance.

characters.name: Dr. Shuttleworth
characters.description: Ditzy Genius: Despite being a child expert, she is easily fooled by Lisa'sPaper-Thin Disguise, and thinks Leni is a volunteer when in fact she'd stumbled into preschool by complete accident. Friend to All Children: She's experienced with children and seems fond of them.

characters.name: Gus Gamesngrub
characters.description: The owner of Gus's Games & Grub. Hidden Depths: "Love Me Tenor" reveals he has an interest in opera singing. Ink-Suit Actor: Looks a lot like Paul Scheer in TLH form, such as sharing his rosy skin, buzz cut, and most notably, the gap in his front teeth. Nice Guy: While Gus can get strict if someone wrongs him, he's otherwise affable and friendly.

characters.name: Bobbie Fletcher
characters.description: One-Steve Limit: Not to be confused with Lori's beloved Boo-Boo Bear, although it'sdownplayedsince her first name is spelled differently. Nice Girl: She's shown to be very nice to her fans. Pet the Dog: Even though Lana had to give up her winning wrapper to Flip, after seeing how quickly the girl fixed her car (claiming that she was faster than her entire pit crew), Bobbie offers her the chance to join her pit crew once she turns 18.

characters.name: Hunter Spector
characters.description: Host of the TV showAcademy ofReallyGoodGhostHunters (ARGGH!) Broken Pedestal: Lincoln and Clyde temporarily lose all admiration of him upon learning the ghost hunting on his show is all an act. Lincoln handles it, but Clyde takes it too hard and throws out everything fantasy related. Nice Character, Mean Actor: Subverted. While his ghost hunting is staged, he truly has a desire to capture real, live ghosts. However, making a TV show means you are restricted in what you can do in terms of time and budget, forcing him to stage his ghost encounters. He also cares for his fans and seems rather polite with his staff (except when they pester him about pay day). Nice Guy: He truly cares for his fans and his crew. Pet the Dog: Stages a ghost hunt with Lincoln to restore Clyde's belief in ghosts.

characters.name: Katherine Mulligan
characters.description: An anchorwoman for Royal Woods News. Ambiguously Brown: Her skin is darker than most Caucasian characters, making her appear mixed-race, possibly half-Latina or half-Afro. However,A Loud House Christmasimplies she's white and just has a tan. Ascended Extra: Has a larger role in "Scoop Snoop" andA Loud House Christmas, and Clyde even has her contact in the latter. Busman's Vocabulary: She talks as if she's giving a news report even when she isn't, much to the annoyance of her camera crew. Given Name Reveal: Her name was revealed in "Scales of Justice".

characters.name: Rip Hardcore
characters.description: Bald Head of Toughness: He's bald and is definitely a macho character. Walking Shirtless Scene: Is never seen with a shirt. Adaptational Attractiveness: Looks a little more ruggedly handsome than his animated self, and even has a mohawk. Ambiguous Situation: His connection to Stanley Bunch. Since they're played by different actors and Rip Hardcore is a title passed on to different people, it's hinted they're separate characters, but Lincoln and Clyde don't find out about Stanley's real identity until after he's fired, suggesting they might be one and the same. Hero Antagonist: In the film, he's merely trying to stop the Sharkodile and save Royal Woods, not realizing it's fake and is being controlled by Lincoln and Clyde.

characters.name: Mick Swagger
characters.description: Luna's favorite musician. Eyes Out of Sight: Much like Lucy, his hair conceals his eyes. Nice Guy: His attitude to Rock and Roll is that it doesn’t matter how good you are, it only matters if you have fun. He even liked the Loud family’s... less-than-stellar performance in ‘House Music’ simply because they all clearly had the time of their lives. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Based onMick Jagger. Older Than They Look: Mick hardly looks like he’s had a “forty year” long career by this point, unless he started when he was very young.

characters.name: SMOOCH
characters.description: A famous four member rockstar band, of whom Lincoln and Clyde are avid fans. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They have not appeared since Season 2 for unknown reasons. The most feasible explanation for their absence is that they're too busy with other concerts outside of Royal Woods to reappear in the show. Expy:Obvious one ofKISS.AlsoThe Rolling Stones. AlsoThe Rolling Stones. Nice Guy:They allow Lincoln, Luna and Clyde to join them up on stage in "For Bros about to Rock", with the lead singer even singing with Lincoln.In "Yes Man", they show up at Lincoln's VIB concert.

characters.name: Theresa Davis
characters.description: The mayor of Royal Woods. Benevolent Boss: She praises Leni for her work as an intern. She also forgives her and gives her credit for one of her campaign ideas in "Electshunned". Berserk Button: Doesn't take it kindly when someone uses her keyboard. Black Boss Lady: Has dark skin and is the mayor of Royal Woods. Genki Girl: She's usually shown to be very peppy and happy.

characters.name: Dr. Alvarez
characters.description: Nice Girl: A very friendly woman, who sincerely wants to get more kids into science. Even when she discovers Lisa had lied about the bone, she still gives Lisa another chance, showing she's not one to hold a grudge. Foil: Alvarez is this to Dr. Carol Linnaeus. Both of them are famous scientists and give Lisa an offer to work with them. But while Dr. Carol Linnaeus pretends to be affable, to get the chance to experiment on Flip Dr. Alvarez is sincerely nice and has no ulterior motives at all and wants Lisa on a science show, so more kids can get into science. Friend to All Children: She is very fond of kids, wanting to find ways in order to help ease them into science. She's also very kind to Lisa and while she isn't happy with her lie about the fake bone, still gives her another chance, by having her as the tour guide of the museum.

characters.name: Exterminator
characters.description: Eccentric Exterminator: He loves killing bugs just alittletoo much. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": He's only referred to as "the exterminator". Fat Bastard: Downplayed. Trying to kill Frank was only doing his job, but he is rude to the kids, calling them "spider huggers". He's also quite fat. Hate Sink: While he's not exactly a villain, and is presumably just doing his job, his cruelty to insects and lack of likable qualities make it clear the audience isn’t supposed to like him. Ignored Aesop: At the end of "Along Came a Sister", he lies about Leni's inspirational speech having changed his worldview.

characters.name: Lord Tetherby
characters.description: The heir to the tetherball fortune and one of the richest men in Royal Woods. When Lincoln wins a ride in a limo, he mistakes him for one of his fellow rich people. Aristocrats Are Evil: Or at least jerkasses. He's a lord and a very unpleasant person. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first he seems like aNice Guy, but if you happen to not be a rich person, he will turn his back on you. The Corrupter: Under his influence, Lincoln becomes aRich Jerk. Evil Counterpart: TheFat Bastardto Pop-Pop/Albert'sBig Fun. They're both chubby elders. But while Pop-Pop enjoys others' company unconditionally, Tetherby only wants to be around people who have a very high status.

characters.name: Sue
characters.description: 0% Approval Rating: Due to hercontrollingand restrictive behavior, none of the seniors respect her and repeatedly call her "Shrew". While Albert initially acts tolerant of Sue, he later ditches any respect he had for her when he goes outside to have fun with Lincoln and is more than happy to see her humiliated by his friends. Battleaxe Nurse: She has the looks and traits to prove it. Control Freak: She runs Sunset Canyon with an iron fist, imposing harsh rules on the seniors, until they force her to let them do what they want. Disproportionate Retribution: She kicks out seniors if they disobey the curfew. Establishing Character Moment: The first thing she's shown doing is kicking out a resident for missing curfew.

characters.name: Michelle and Doug
characters.description: Big Bad Duumvirate: They always work together and they are both equally meddlesome and pushy. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first, they seem like decent folk. As of Act II... Executive Meddling: In-universe example. They try to completely change Luna's image from a rocker girl to a pop star just because pop music is more popular. Hate Sink: While it is unclear who is the more unlikable of the two, both of them are as every bit as slimy, meddlesome, and shallow as one can assume executives of the music industry to be. Jerkass: They are both dishonest, pushy, and manipulative.

characters.name: Jeff and Carly Miller
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: They might seem like nice people at first, but they're revealed to be spies working for the evil organization S.U.S.P.E.N.S.E. Breaking Old Trends: In a show where most of the "villains" are nothing more than bullies or jerks, they stand out as being the first antagonists in the show to be legitimately evil. Does Not Like Spam:Exaggerated. They do NOT like cherries, to the point they want to destroy them altogether. Evil All Along: As it turns out, Lincoln was right about them being evil all along. Evil Counterpart: They both resemble a slightly younger versions of Lynn Sr. and Rita. However, while Lynn Sr. and Rita are good parents (occasional immaturity and incompetence aside), Jeff and Carly are evil and devious enough to try and cripple the economy of an innocent town.

characters.name: Dr. Carol Linnaeus
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She initially presents herself as an affable woman who offers to pay Flip for agreeing to let her study him, but her true colors are shown not long after, when Lisa spies on her cruelly experimenting on Flip. Evil Counterpart: To Lisa. They are both highly, intelligent scientists who tend to do dangerous experiments. The only difference is that Lisa still has compassion for other living beings while Carol risks the health and safety of her subjects without compunction. For Science!: She intends to launch Flip into space without a spacesuit and doesn't care whether he gets killed in the attempt. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: She wears square-rimmed glasses and is nothing but heartless. Hate Sink: Just look at the other tropes describing her.

characters.name: VicMcGillicuddy
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: He's a recurring villain but top villains like Morag, Joyce, andFifimake him look like a typicalVillain of the Week. Bullying a Dragon: He tries pushing around the Loud family, even though said family includes Lynn and Lola, two of the show's biggest powerhouses. Had the two not wanted a vacation, he would've been in for the beating of a lifetime. The Corruptor: Vic acts as one towards Mayor Davis as he tries to get her to say horrible things about Leni as an attempt to keep her status as Mayor. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He’s very close to his pet Gila Monster, Gilly. Evil Is Petty: From the 17-year old Leni, 12-year olds Lincoln and Clyde, and the other Loud kids, not even kids are safe from his insults and scams.

characters.name: Joyce Crandall
characters.description: 0% Approval Rating: It goes without saying that her plans for Royal Woods don't make her a popular figure among the locals. Ambition Is Evil: What does she hope to gain from flooding Royal Woods? Getting promoted to Oversecretary. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: Can be seen as this to Morag fromThe Loud House Movie. Both are the femaleBig Badsof special episodes (Morag for the movie, Joyce for a half-hour special), but also near-complete opposites.Morag is a slightly dark-skinned Scottish royal housekeeper with dark, slightly graying hair. Joyce is a pale-skinned American politician with red hair.Whereas Morag used a fire-breathing dragon in an attempt to wreck and drive everyone away from Loch Loud, Joyce seeks to bust a dam and flood Royal Woods to create a sixth Great Lake.While Morag kept her plans secret until she was caught in a lie the second she got what she wanted, Joyce is completely unsubtle about what she wants to do and how callous she was about it long before she got around to it.Morag wanted to forcibly overthrow Lincoln and become Duchess of Loch Loud for peace and quiet, while Joyce carried out her scheme in hope that she would attain her ambition of getting a legal promotion within Michigan's state government.Morag's scheme revolved entirely around the Loud family. Joyce, on the other hand, didn't have anything to do with the Louds specifically, only affecting them as a side effect to her intentions. Morag is a slightly dark-skinned Scottish royal housekeeper with dark, slightly graying hair. Joyce is a pale-skinned American politician with red hair. Whereas Morag used a fire-breathing dragon in an attempt to wreck and drive everyone away from Loch Loud, Joyce seeks to bust a dam and flood Royal Woods to create a sixth Great Lake.

characters.name: Guy Grazer
characters.description: Ascended Extra: First made a cameo appearance in "Present Tense", then became the main antagonist of "Dine and Bash" and "Forks and Knives Out". Caustic Critic: He's introduced roasting a female chef student about her and her sauce being weak. And it only gets worse from here. Large Ham: As befits a Gordon Ramsay expy. Let's You and Him Fight: The primary point of his "Kitchen Combat" show. He deliberately seeks to invoke this when Lincoln, Lynn Sr., Ronnie Anne, and Rosa compete on the show, outright trying to get them to be antagonistic to each other. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Has the personality ofGordon Ramsayand the looks of Guy Fieri.

characters.name: Hugh
characters.description: A British community college student who Lincoln hires as his tutor. He ends up getting the unwanted attention of nearly all of Lincoln's sisters... and dad. Anachronism Stew: He rides a penny farthing bicycle. Camp Straight: He wears pink, is very mindful of his appearance, but is wigged out by the advances of the Loud girls... And their father. Chick Magnet: Catches the eyes of all of the Loud girls (except Lily). Clueless Chick-Magnet: Subverted. At first he has no idea the Loud Girls are interested in him but that quickly changes, to his embarrassment.

characters.name: Ms.DiMartino
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: While she has tan skin and a vaguely Hispanic surname, it's unclear whether she's supposed to be a Latina or not. It's equally plausable, however, that she's Italian. Beauty Equals Goodness: She's considered attractive in-universe and is a nice teacher to her students. Distracted by the Sexy: Invokes this in her male students. Dude Magnet: She accidentally swoons the whole male student body of the school, including Lincoln and Clyde. Even the Girls Want Her: Luna Loud joins her brother and all his male classmates in finding her to be beautiful.

characters.name: Jerry Kling
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: He is laid-back, friendly farmer who gets along with the Loud family,is a spokesperson for a brand of cherries that Lynn Sr. likes using and he even offers them to stay in his hotel room when they find out that the reservation for their room expired. Foil: While the two have never crossed paths, Jerry Kling can be considered this to Lord Tetherby. Lord Tetherby is a toxic and unpleasant man who is blatant about his wealth and looks down on anyone and anything he considers to be beneath him. Contrast that with Jerry Kling, who at first comes off as an ordinary cherry farmer, but turns out to be not onlySecretly Wealthy, but also nothing short of generous to the middle-class Louds. Nice Guy: When the Loud family helps him with his flat tire, he thanks them by giving them some of his cherries.Then at the end of the episode, he offers them to stay in his hotel room after they find out their own room has been taken by someone else. Punny Name: His name, Jerry King, is a pun ofCherry King, a brand of cherries that he is a spokesperson for. Uncle Pennybags: The end of the episode "Tripped!" reveals that he isa spokesperson for a popular brand of cherries and rich enough to reserve the entire top floor of a hotel. Despite that, he is nothing but nice and generous to the Louds.

characters.name: Calvin Coconuts
characters.description: Anti-Villain: While he does steal Mr. Coconuts and tries to prevent the Louds from recovering him, he only did it so he could be reunited with what he sees as his son. Passing the Torch: He's a retired puppet maker and performer and hands Mr. Coconuts back to Luan, telling her to make sure Mr. Coconuts can share his talents with the world.

characters.name: Gertie / The Gopher
characters.description: Boy Jordan's grandmother. In her youth, she was a supervillain known as the Gopher who frequently tangled with Myrtle. Acrofatic: She's gained weight in her elderly years, but is just as agile as in her youth. Animal-Themed Superbeing: The Gopher specializes in digging tunnels around anywhere she can be. Formerly Fit: In her youth, she used to be quite slim and agile. She's gained weight by the present, but she's still just as agile. Heel–Face Turn: In the present, she's left her days as the Gopher behind and genuinely wants to do good as founder of G.A.B. and a good grandmother to Boy Jordan.

characters.name: Angus
characters.description: Actor Allusion: He's not thefirst character named Angusto be voiced by David Tennant. His catchphrase, "Blow my bagpipes!", is very similar to ScroogeMcDuck's "Bless me bagpipes!" inDuckTales (2017). Affectionate Gesture to the Head: He gives Lincoln one shortly before the latter returns to Royal Woods with his family. Catchphrase: "Blow my bagpipes!" The Conscience: When Lincoln getsAcquired Situational Narcissismfrom being the Duke, Angus serves as this to him, reminding him his deeds are for the people, not himself, and successfully convinces him such with just a few words. The Good King:After Lincolnpasses the title of Duke onto him, Angus rules Loch Loud benevolently, with the help of the Louds' 1600s ancestors.

characters.name: Morag
characters.description: The main antagonist of the film. She's the cantankerous caretaker of the Louds' castle. Her ancestor, former caretaker Aggie, had initially managed to rid Scotland of the Louds in order to achieve some peace and quiet. Ambiguously Brown: She's a Scottish woman, but has dark skin. Ax-Crazy: Although she doesn't act insane all the time like most examples, Morag still establishes herself to be absolutely crazy, especially when vehemently seeking out to accomplish the success of herevil plans. Bathing Beauty: Downplayed in thebeautypart. She's notthatmuch of a looker, but she is introduced while taking relaxing baths. Big Bad: She is the first genuinely evil antagonist of the franchise.

characters.name: Aggie
characters.description: Bad People Abuse Animals: She called Lolo the dragon a "monstrous pea-brained cretin". The Corrupter:With the Dragon Stone and Royal Scepter, she and Morag are this to dragons. Evil Sorceress:It was she who createdthe Dragon Stone. Greater-Scope Villain:AndSmall Role, Big Impact. As the one who drove the 1600s Louds away in the first place, thus resulting in the present day's generation of Louds having the lives they do in Royal Woods, she is responsible for everything that happens in theThe Loud Housefranchise. Karma Houdini:She is never known to have received any comeuppance for driving away the Louds.

characters.name: Lela
characters.description: All Animals Are Dogs: When the Louds first meet her as a baby, she playfully roughhouses with Angus and licks him like a puppy. The Chooser of the One: As a dragon of Loch Loud, she has the ultimate authority to deem someone worthy of being the Duke of Loch Loud. Case in point:the one she returned the crown to after Morag was defeated was Lincoln. Our Dragons Are Different: Lela shows that not only are dragons actually real, like Lana speculated, but they seemingly grow older by how much they eat: during the course of the movie, she goes from about Lily's size to twice her size just by eating some burritos,and by the climax she's about as big as the former dragon of the family, Lolo.

characters.name: Scott
characters.description: Doomed by Canon: Not Scott himself, but his relationship with Leni. Seeing as how the movie is set between Seasons 4 and 5, and it came outafterthe Season 5 episode "Undercover Mom" (which shows Leni crushing on a different guy), it's obvious his relationship with Leni doesn't last long. Satellite Love Interest: We do see he's also into fashion, but outside of that he definitely has no character.

characters.name: Lucille Loud
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation:She is carrying Lucy when she, her parents, sisters, and Angus spot an unconscious Lincoln after he'd crashed into the castle's entrance with Morag and Lela, but is mysteriously absent once Morag prepares to incinerate the Loud family as well as Angus, controlling Lela. It's possible she went to recruit her own parents and siblings to help out, only for Lincoln himself to do it for them in the nick of time. Big Damn Heroes: She discovers Aggie's book and the page with the dragon mind control spell, allowing her to realize Morag is the true threat and Lincoln is innocent. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: Although very little is known about their relationship, it's implied she's the responsible to the ancestral Duke's foolish, asshe's the one who has to get him tosurrender his crown to their mind controlled dragon for their family's safety. Although, it was less "convince" and more "inform of what needs to be done",as the Duke actually listened and heeded her words rather than actually argue against them and make things worse. Friendly Ghost: She is very helpful towards the living generation of the Loud family, and appears to be more quirky and fun than Lucy. Our Ghosts Are Different: Lucille is surrounded by an ethereal blue light, and can choose whether to be solid or intangible at will.

characters.name: The Duke
characters.description: Lincoln Loud's ancestral double, and the former ruler of Loch Loud. Badass Cape: He wears a cape, and is a child monarch who wields a sword and rides a dragon. Big Good: This is how Angus describes him. Despite seemingly being the foolish sibling to Lucille's responsible sibling,he's touted as being the most special Loud of all time, whose name was known far and wide(and, ironically, isn't spoken at all in the film), deeds were noble, and heart was stout. Do Not Taunt Cthulhu:When Lolo, actually controlled by Aggie, confronts him and deems him no longer worthy of being Duke, heangrily commandsher to let him and his family back to Loch Loud, only to nearly get incinerated. 11th-Hour Ranger:He, and the rest of his family sans Lucille, only really factors into the present day plot at the end, to further approve of Angus becoming the new Duke.

characters.name: Xander Coddington
characters.description: The main antagonist ofA Really Haunted Loud House, Xander is introduced as a new kid at Royal Woods Middle School with a huge following of fans (known as the Xander Nation). Canon Foreigner: Only exists in the continuity ofThe Really Loud House. Captain Ersatz: He's pretty much Chandler's live-action counterpart.

characters.name: Xander Nation
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Johnny was first seen inThe Really Loud Houseproper, where he has a minor role in the episode "Ro-Bro" as the catalyst for Ro-Bros creation. Here, he's a member of the Xander Nation and gets more screentime as a result. Mooks: Since the Xander Nation consists of followers of Xander, most of them aren't exactly fully fleshed out as a result and are simply characterized as his minions.

characters.name: Punguari/Shara
characters.description: Big Bad Friend: She starts out befriending Ronnie Anne in order to obtain The Mask of Many Faces and restore her physical form and godhood.She loses the 'Big Bad' partonce shelearns the truth beind her banishment, and helps Ronnie Anne and her family to stop Ucumu. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: She's this toMorag.Both have relatives shown from centuries ago (Punguari's parents, Morag's relative Aggie), both pretended to befriend the main protagonists and manipulated them to get what they both wanted (for Punguari, she took the form of human alias Shara and manipulated Ronnie Anne into getting the Mask of Many Faces; for Morag, she manipulated the Loud sisters into showing off their talents to Loch Loud, making Lincoln feel like he's in their shadow again and then manipulating him into taking Lela for a ride, so that she can brainwash the dragon and cause damage to Loch Loud, making the villagers hate Lincoln, so she can take the crown for herself) and both briefly ended up in a high position of power (for Punguari, she makes herself a full goddess; for Morag, she crowns herself as duchess).The only difference between the two is that Punguari had aHeel Realizationand made aHeel–Face Turnto stop the true Big Bad, while Morag remains as the Big Bad and has a very petty motivation. Godhood Seeker: An interesting variation. Punguari is already a demigod who wants to become a full god earlier than her parents will allow her. This motivation drives the plot of the movie. Heel–Face Turn:After discovering the real truth behind her parents' disappearence, she sees the error of her ways, and decides to help Ronnie Anne save all of Mexico from Ucumu, and seal him off with the remains of her temple. Mirror Character: Although she turns out to be a good person at heart, Punguari, in a way, represents what Ronnie Anne could've become had the latter chosen not to give up her pranking ways and/or chosen her own wants over her mom.

characters.name: Sisiki
characters.description: Good Parents: Despite how callous it seems for her to turn her daughter into a mountain,she was actually looking out for her daughter, protecting her from being killed by Ucumu. Greater-Scope Paragon: She, along with her husband Chipiri, are sworn protectors of the Chancla Warriors tribe.And her role in protecting Punguari from Ucumu ensures that her daughter, along with Ronnie Anne and her family, can stop theEvil Godonce and for all.

characters.name: Chipiri
characters.description: Good Parents: Despite dismissing Punguari's desire to be a full god, he does care about his daughter, Greater-Scope Paragon: He, along with his wifi Sisiki, are sworn protectors of the Chancla Warriors tribe.

characters.name: Dr. Rufus Dufus
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: "Roofy-Floofy" from his wife. Asshole Victim: He accidentally gets launched into space. But given all the evil he committed in the past and that he tried to take over the world, onlyFifi'stears are shed. French Jerk: Implied. He claims his name is French at least. The Lost Lenore: A villainous example for Fifi. His demise is the reason behind Fifi's campaign of vengeance against Myrtle. The Napoleon: He is only a small guy, about half the size of most adults on the show, and a villain who wants toTake Over the World.

characters.name: Ham Hand
characters.description: Artificial Limbs: Dr. Dufus gave him a hammer as a replacement for the hand he lost in a wrestling match. The Brute: Relies soley on his huge size and strength. The Dragon: To Dr. Dufus in the past and Fifi in the present. The Fighting Narcissist: He absolutely loves his hair, which he frequently praises himself for; Myrtle would use this to her advantage when fighting him. Ink-Suit Actor: Like his voice actor, Paul Wight (also known as the Big Show), Ham Hand was a professional wrestler in his own right, but the loss of his hand would lead to him falling from grace and turning to a life of crime.

characters.name: Flop Phillipini
characters.description: Dub Name Change: In the Polish dub, he's renamed Flap... which his English name is misspelled at times in TV broadcasts' closed-captioning. I Have Many Names:Just like Flip,Flop has a penchant of adopting a variety of aliases to fit the various jobs he has. Non-Human Sidekick: He's always accompanied by his pet crab, Ceviche. Offscreen Moment of Awesome:Somehow, he managed to capture two dangerous supervillains and bring them to justice. Uncanny Family Resemblance: Looksexactly identicalto his cousin, Flip. They even have the same voice!

characters.name: Duncan
characters.description: Black-and-White Morality: Since he's had little to no intimate interaction with humans, he holds this view toward them.However, as he witnesses firsthand just how far Lincoln is willing to go to fix Christmas, he comes to realize that this isn't the case. Character Development: He starts the film with a black and white view on naughty and nice, believing it's only determined by data.In the climax, he realizes no one is completely naughty or nice and being both makes one human. Deuteragonist: While Lincoln is still the protagonist, the story is just as much about Duncan's perspective on naughty and nice changing as it is about Lincoln. I Owe You My Life: He gratefully yet sadly thanks Lincoln ashe mourns hisHeroic Sacrificeinsaving his life from getting turned into a cookie.Duncan:I can’t believe you did that… You saved me… Manly Tears:Sheds these as he is mourning Lincoln'sHeroic Sacrifice.

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: Bad Santa: He's gone naughty after Lincoln hacks the North Pole. Evil Costume Switch: He ditches his iconic getup in favor of a more rugged look, complete with replacing his hat with a dark wig. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His naughty design and voice may or may not be a reference toJack Black. Not Himself: He's normally fair (if a little stern) guy and love Christmas. But due to Lincoln messing with the computer that judge people naughty or nice. He gets affected and acting malicious and hostile until Lincoln and Duncan can fix the problem. Unseen No More: He's been alluded to in the main series several times before finally showing up in the flesh in the thirdLoud Housefilm.
